method.title: E. coli Transformation with Plasmid DNA (Heat Shock and Plating)
method.summary: Competent E. coli cells are mixed with plasmid DNA by flicking and briefly chilled on ice. They are heat-shocked at 42°C (the procedure says water bath, the equipment list says thermal cycler) and returned to ice. Culture is then spread on a selective LB agar plate, and the plate is inverted.

method.title: Passaging Adherent Cells in a Biosafety Cabinet (PBS Wash, Trypsin-EDTA Detachment, Reseeding)
method.summary: Adherent cells in a 10 cm dish are taken from the incubator, washed with PBS, detached with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA, neutralised with complete medium and pipetted into a single-cell suspension. The suspension is moved to a conical tube, reseeded into a new 10 cm dish with fresh medium, distributed by cross-pattern rocking, and returned to the incubator. Note the document's inconsistencies: a 15 ml tube in the equipment list versus 50 ml in the procedure, and a calculated ~2 ml for a 1:3 split versus 5 ml dispensed. Step 17, the split volume calculation, is mental work, so it is not a separate observable step; it is noted under the reseeding step.
